problem: At compact viewport sizes, opening the navigation sidebar moves focus into its search field but leaves keyboard focus able to reach the page behind the overlay.
desired_outcome: The compact sidebar behaves as a named modal navigation drawer for keyboard and assistive technology users, while desktop navigation retains its current non-modal behavior.
user_journey: A staff member activates the compact navigation button.
Focus moves to the navigation search field and remains in the open drawer while tabbing in either direction.
The staff member closes the drawer with Escape or the backdrop and focus returns to the opener.
On desktop, the sidebar remains normal page navigation without modal focus containment.

current_evidence.claim: At the pre-change AppLayout SHA, the component focused the sidebar search on open, restored the invoking element on close, and handled Escape, but the open compact sidebar had no dialog semantics or Tab containment.
An existing appointment drawer test provides a local reference for wrapping Tab, recovering focus, restoring focus, and yielding to a nested dialog.

The Boolean inert bindings omit the attribute when inactive; the focused component test asserts that the sidebar is not inert while open or on desktop and that the background is inert while the compact drawer is open.

The focused AppLayout component suite passed all four cases. Assertions cover compact focus containment and restoration, reverse-Tab recovery from outside, exclusion of hidden and disabled targets including a CSS-hidden ancestor, backdrop and Escape close, desktop non-modal behavior, nested-dialog keyboard ownership, and the empty-controls fallback.
current_evidence.source: Node 22.23.2: pnpm --filter @cvg-his-v2/spa exec vitest run --config vitest.config.ts tests/unit/AppLayoutCompactNavigation.test.ts (4/4, exit 0)

current_evidence.claim: The SPA Vue and TypeScript project check passed after using typed Boolean inert states.
The existing SPA Playwright config supports Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit but auto-starts API and SPA servers on ports 3111/3112 and binds database URLs.

unknowns.falsification: Complete manual assistive-technology review on the approved browser and screen-reader matrix.

constraints: Keep navigation authorization and route ownership unchanged.
Add no dependencies and make no API, database, or network changes.
Preserve Escape, backdrop close, initial focus, desktop navigation, and focus restoration.
Do not start the Playwright runtime because its config opens dedicated API/SPA ports and may bind database services.

render_environment.server: Static SPA assets; application APIs remain outside this interaction change.
render_environment.client: AppLayout owns responsive drawer interaction and focus lifecycle.
render_environment.hydration: No SSR hydration boundary is used by this Vite SPA.

browser_targets: Existing Playwright SPA projects list Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit; they were not run in this constrained local round.
device_input_constraints: Pointer input: backdrop close remains available.
Screen-reader virtual navigation requires later browser and manual review.
ux_invariants: Opening from compact layout focuses the sidebar search field.
Keyboard focus cannot tab into the background while the drawer is open.
Escape and backdrop close preserve current close behavior and restore the opener focus.
Desktop sidebar navigation is not exposed or handled as a modal dialog.
accessibility_invariants: The open compact drawer has role dialog, aria-modal=true, and a stable accessible name.
Tab and Shift+Tab wrap over enabled, visible descendants of the sidebar.
The compact skip link, header, and workspace are inert while open; the backdrop is aria-hidden and removed from sequential focus while preserving pointer close.
A nested dialog retains ownership of its own keyboard handling.
data_invariants: Sidebar permissions and route filtering are unchanged.
No clinical or business data is read, changed, or cached by this interaction.

selected_pattern: Existing aside with conditional modal semantics, background inertness, and local Tab containment
selection_rationale: The sidebar already owns the responsive open state and focus restoration, so it is the smallest coherent behavior boundary.
The compact overlay is modal while open; desktop navigation remains ordinary navigation.
The change adds no package, API, database, or persisted state.

component_boundaries.name: AppLayout compact navigation drawer
component_boundaries.extraction_driver: The application shell already owns the shared navigation and responsive focus lifecycle; no new component extraction is justified.
component_boundaries.accessibility_contract: Named modal dialog while compact-open; focus stays inside; Escape/backdrop close and restore focus; nested dialog retains its keyboard contract.

data_fetching_contract.deduplication: Existing session permission fetch is unchanged.

mutation_semantics.rollback: Closing restores only focus and the previous persisted sidebar state.

loading_behavior: No change to existing navigation permission loading.
empty_behavior: If the sidebar has no focusable child, the sidebar container receives focus and remains the focus boundary.
recovery_behavior: Escape and backdrop close remain available; the opener receives focus if it is still connected.
responsive_behavior: Modal behavior applies only at the existing max-width 860px breakpoint while the sidebar is open.
keyboard_focus_behavior: Open focuses search; Tab/Shift+Tab wrap within visible enabled sidebar descendants; Escape closes; close returns to the original opener; desktop has no trap.
assistive_behavior: Open compact sidebar exposes a named modal dialog, makes the skip link, header, and workspace inert, and hides the non-focusable backdrop from the accessibility tree while preserving pointer close. Manual screen-reader review is required before an accessibility acceptance claim.
motion_behavior: No new animation; existing reduced-motion scrolling behavior is unchanged.
